name: Alona Beach and Tawala
tagline: Bohol's tourist strip, dive shops and beach bars
description: Alona Beach in barangay Tawala on Panglao is the busiest strip in the province, a short arc of white sand backed by dive shops, resorts, smoothie cafes and beach bars. The lanes behind it hold guesthouses, scooter rentals and the island's main coworking spaces. Fibre internet is strongest here.
bestFor: Nomads who want beach, coworking and other travellers within walking distance
pros: The only real nomad community in the province
Best internet, cafes and coworking on the island
Diving, island hopping and rentals all on the doorstep
cons: Tourist pricing on food and accommodation
Beach bars and karaoke run loud into the night
The beach itself is crowded and narrow at high tide

name: Doljo and Danao, Panglao
tagline: Quiet west-coast beaches ten minutes from Alona
description: The western tip of Panglao around Doljo and Danao beaches is a stretch of coconut groves, small villas and low-key resorts on wide, mostly empty sand. There are a handful of cafes but no strip, so you ride a scooter to Alona for anything social. Sunsets face straight out to sea.
bestFor: Nomads who want beach living without the noise and can ride a scooter
pros: Wide, uncrowded beaches with real sunsets
Villas and long-stay rentals cost less than Alona
Ten minutes by scooter to the Alona amenities
cons: A scooter is essential, nothing is walkable
Very few restaurants, cafes or shops nearby
Internet is more variable than on the Alona strip

name: Dauis
tagline: The causeway town between Panglao and the city
description: Dauis sits on the northeast corner of Panglao island at the causeway bridges to Tagbilaran, built around its old coral-stone church and the Hinagdanan Cave area. It is residential rather than touristy, with local markets, a growing set of cafes and quick access in both directions.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who want island rents and city errands both in reach
pros: Ten minutes to Tagbilaran malls and hospitals
Local prices for food, markets and rentals
Still on Panglao island with beaches close by
cons: No beach in the town centre itself
Causeway traffic backs up at peak hours
Little in the way of nomad or expat social life

name: Tagbilaran City
tagline: The provincial capital, malls, hospitals and cheap rent
description: Tagbilaran is Bohol's small capital, a working port city with the island's malls, hospitals, banks, ferry pier and government offices packed into a few busy streets. It is not scenic, but it is where you sort visas, medical care and serious shopping, and long-term rents are the cheapest in the province.
bestFor: Budget nomads and anyone who needs reliable services more than a sea view
pros: Cheapest apartments and food in Bohol
Hospitals, immigration, banks and malls all here
Ferry pier connects to Cebu several times daily
cons: Noisy, hot and congested with tricycle traffic
No beach and very little charm
Almost no cafe or coworking scene for laptops

name: Baclayon
tagline: Old coastal town with a heritage church and calm water
description: Baclayon sits on the coast just east of Tagbilaran, an old town built around one of the oldest stone churches in the Philippines. The coastal road is lined with mangroves, small resorts and family homes, and the seafront is calm rather than swimmable. Life here is slow and firmly local.
bestFor: Nomads on a long stay who want quiet coastal living and local prices
pros: Very cheap long-term houses and rooms
Quiet coastal setting close to Tagbilaran services
Easy jump-off point for the Loboc river and Chocolate Hills
cons: The shoreline is mangrove and reef, not swimming beach
You need a scooter for almost everything
No nomad community and minimal English-language services
